1. Core Clinical Tension: A 23-year-old male presents with intermittent passage of small, white, balloon-like, grape-sized structures in the urine (hydatiduria) and a non-functioning cystic mass completely replacing the right kidney with involvement of the ureter. Differentiating primary renal hydatid disease from multicystic dysplastic kidney, multilocular cystic nephroma, or cystic renal cell carcinoma is critical, especially given normal baseline labs and absent eosinophilia.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The admission breakpoint concludes after clinical history of passing urinary structures, physical examination, normal laboratory workup (normal CBC, absence of eosinophilia, normal renal function), plain chest radiograph, and abdominal ultrasound/CT imaging showing multiseptate cystic replacement of the right kidney and upper ureter with non-excretion of contrast. Histopathological analysis of expelled urinary membranes and nephroureterectomy specimen represent confirmatory testing.
3. Differential Distinctions: Multilocular cystic renal cell carcinoma or cystic nephroma can present with a non-functioning multiseptated renal mass, but spontaneous passage of intact membranous structures in urine indicates communication with the pelvicalyceal system and parasite-derived cuticles. Secondary renal echinococcosis from primary hepatic or pulmonary disease was ruled out by entirely normal liver ultrasound and normal chest radiography, establishing primary urinary tract hydatid disease.
case_prompt:
A 23-year-old male presents with a three-month history of intermittent passage of small, white, balloon-like, grape-sized structures in his urine during micturition. He reports no dysuria, gross hematuria, flank pain, or fever.

On physical examination, his vital signs are normal. Abdominal examination reveals a soft, non-tender abdomen with no palpable flank lump or organomegaly. The remainder of the systemic examination is entirely normal.

Routine laboratory investigations are unremarkable, showing normal complete blood count without eosinophilia and normal renal function tests (blood urea nitrogen and serum creatinine). Plain chest radiography (posteroanterior view) is normal.

Abdominal ultrasonography reveals a multiseptate cystic mass replacing the right kidney; the liver parenchyma is normal with no cystic lesions. Abdominal computed tomography (CT) confirms an extensive multilocular cystic lesion involving the entire right kidney and upper ureter, with complete replacement of normal renal architecture and absence of contrast excretion from the right kidney.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Cystic renal cell carcinoma or multilocular cystic nephroma
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the extensive multiseptate cystic mass completely replacing the right renal parenchyma with loss of contrast excretion; however, gross and microscopic analysis of the passed urinary vesicles revealed parasitic laminated and germinal layers rather than neoplastic epithelium.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: The CT scan revealed a cystic lesion in the right kidney and upper ureter [Figure 1]. The whole right kidney was replaced by the cystic mass.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Disseminated or secondary echinococcosis with primary pulmonary or hepatic cysts
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered because the kidney is an uncommon site of primary hydatid disease; ruled out as primary extra-renal foci were excluded by normal chest radiography and normal liver ultrasonography.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: X-ray chest P-A view was normal. The USG abdomen revealed multiseptate cyst in the right kidney; liver was normal.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Gross examination of the passed urinary structures revealed a 2-cm membranous cyst with histopathology showing outer acellular laminated and inner germinal layers, and right nephroureterectomy confirmed a kidney transformed into a bag of cysts containing multiple daughter cysts tracking down the ureter.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Gross examination of a single balloon-like structure in the urine revealed a membranous cyst measuring around 2 cm; histopathology showed an outer laminated layer with an inner germinal layer. The laminated structure was consistent with a hydatid cyst.

editor_comments: Case prompt strictly describes the gross patient-reported passage of balloon-like structures in urine without disclosing the histological finding of laminated layers or hydatid cyst. Cross-sectional imaging findings included up to the point of surgical planning.
